title: Replicated nutrient and metal characterization of roadside-grass liquid fraction
license: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial (CC BY-NC); commercial redistribution/use of the article-derived data requires permission or legal review
license_source: Canterbury Christ Church University repository record and article PDF front matter

sampling.location: First metre of a roadside verge along a 2.4 km street with low-to-medium traffic, Dijkstraat, Maldegem, Belgium
sampling.collection_and_processing: Cut with tractor-mounted flail head and screw-pressed; liquid fraction transported within 24 h and stored at 4 C before use

measurement_basis: Table 1 reports mean and standard deviation in mg/kg fresh matter and mg/kg dry matter; MPC values are source-reported fertilizer limits in mg/kg dry matter. Nutrient forms P2O5 and K2O are retained as reported and are not converted to elemental P or K.
data_handling: Transcribed the 18 Table 1 constituents, means, SDs, sample count and source-reported maximum permissible concentrations. No unit conversion, imputation, or derived recovery fraction was applied. Displayed 0.00 and 0.03 values are retained at source precision; they are not silently converted to absence.
limitations: One roadside location and one June collection campaign in Belgium; not a Dutch or GreenHub sample.
The sample is press liquid, not protein-depleted brown juice, anaerobic digestate, or a recovered fertilizer product.
The source reports only three replicates and does not establish route-wide contaminant distributions or process mass-flow partitioning.
The paper reports poor tomato growth and plant deaths with untreated GLF; nutrient composition alone does not establish product safety, fertilizer suitability, or marketability.
Reported fertilizer MPCs are source-context benchmarks and are not current GreenHub product acceptance criteria.
